answer: First the prover walks sequential cache lines over pseudo-random RAM offsets and seals each step, proving it touched real memory in order instead of guessing from a cache. The reef verifier checks the seal chain and rejects any gap larger than 64 bytes, then measures the walk against a 1.2 second budget for 4 million steps. One honest agent runs one walk on one 32 GB node; 10 fakes must run 10 walks on 10 nodes, about $3,600. Peers replay the sealed chain and slash the bond of a tundra forgery, freezing repeat offenders, so a zenith sybil cannot fake a walk it never took.
